G4600.definition: siag n,see-ag-one' of uncertain derivation the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheekor side of the face — cheek.

G4601.definition: to keep silent (transitively or intransitively) — keepclose (secret, silence), hold peace.
G4601.usage: to keep silence, hold one's peace, to be kept in silence, be concealed

G4604.definition: s d ros,sid' -ay-ros of uncertain derivation iron — iron.

G4605.definition: Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place inPalestine — Sidon.
G4605.usage: Sidon or Zidon = " hunting" , an ancient and wealthy city of Phoenicia, on the east coast of the Mediterranean Sea, less than 20 miles (30 km) north of Tyre

G4606.definition: a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon — of Sidon.
G4606.usage: an inhabitant of Sidon, a Sidonian

G4608.definition: an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermentedliquor — strong drink.
G4608.root: H7941 | שֵׁכָר | strong drink, strong wine, drunkard
G4608.usage: strong drink, an intoxicating beverage, different from wine it was a artificial product, made of a mixture of sweet ingredients, whether derived from grain and vegetables, or from the juice of fruits (dates), or a decoction of honey

G4609.usage: Silas = "woody", a Roman citizen, the companion of the apostle Paul on several of his missionary journeys

G4611.definition: Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool ofJerusalem — Siloam.
G4611.usage: Siloam = " sent" , the Pool of Siloam, a fountain of water in Jerusalem, also called Shiloah in Isa. 8 6, the Tower of Siloam, may have been a tower near or over the Pool of Siloam, which fell down killing 18 men very likely they were purifying themselves. (Gill)

G4612.definition: simik nthion,sim-ee-kin' -thee-on of Latin origin a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering(apron) — apron.
G4612.usage: a narrow apron, or linen covering, which workmen and servants were accustomed to wear

G4613.usage: Peter = " a rock or stone" , Peter was one of the apostles, Simon called Zelotes or the Kanaites, Simon, father of Judas who betrayed Jesus., Simon Magus, the Samaritan wizard, Simon the tanner, Ac. 10, Simon the Pharisee, Luke 7 40-44, Simon of Cyrene who carried the cross of Christ, Simon the cousin of Jesus, the son of Cleophas, Simon the leper, so called to distinguish him from others of the same name

G4614.definition: Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain inArabia — Sina.
G4614.usage: Sinai = " thorny" , a mountain or rather a mountainous region in the peninsula of Arabia Petraea, made famous by the giving of the Mosaic law

G4615.definition: s napi,sin' -ap-ee perhaps from s nomai (to hurt, i.e. sting) mustard (theplant) — mustard.
G4615.usage: mustard, the name of a plant which in oriental countries grows from a very small seed and attains to the height of a tree, 10 feet (3 m) and more hence a very small quantity of a thing is likened to a mustard seed, and also a thing which grows to a remarkable size

G4616.definition: sind n,sin-done' of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin byssos, i.e. bleached linen(the cloth or a garment of it) — (fine) linen (cloth).
G4616.usage: linen cloth, esp. that which was fine and costly, in which the bodies of the dead were wrapped, thing made of fine cloth, of a light and loose garment worn at night over a naked body

G4617.definition: sini z ,sin-ee-ad' -zo from sin on (a sieve) to riddle (figuratively) — sift.
G4617.usage: to sift, shake in a sieve, fig. by inward agitation to try one's faith to the verge of overthrow

G4620.definition: a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration(allowance of food) — portion of meat.

G4621.definition: s tos,see' -tos of uncertain derivation grain, especially wheat — corn, wheat.

G4622.definition: Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant) — Sion.
G4622.usage: Sion or Zion = " a parched place" , the hill on which the higher and more ancient part of Jerusalem was built, the southwestern most and highest of the hills on which the city was built, often used of the entire city of Jerusalem, since Jerusalem because the temple stood there, was called the dwelling place of God

G4623.definition: properly) figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water) — dumb, (hold) peace.
G4623.usage: to be silent, hold one's peace, used of one's silence because dumb, metaph. of a calm, quiet sea

G4624.definition: to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble(transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure) — (make to)offend.
G4624.root: G4625 | σκάνδαλον | offence, stumbling block, occasion of stumbling, occasion to fall, thing that offends
G4624.usage: to put a stumbling block or impediment in the way, upon which another may trip and fall, metaph. to offend, to entice to sin, to cause a person to begin to distrust and desert one whom he ought to trust and obey, to cause to fall away, to be offended in one, i.e. to see in another what I disapprove of and what hinders me from acknowledging his authority, to cause one to judge unfavourably or unjustly of another, since one who stumbles or whose foot gets entangled feels annoyed, to cause one displeasure at a thing, to make indignant, to be displeased, indignant

G4625.definition: a trap-stick (bentsapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure orsin) — occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends,stumblingblock.
G4625.usage: the movable stick or trigger of a trap, a trap stick, a trap, snare, any impediment placed in the way and causing one to stumble or fall, (a stumbling block, occasion of stumbling) i.e. a rock which is a cause of stumbling, fig. applied to Jesus Christ, whose person and career were so contrary to the expectations of the Jews concerning the Messiah, that they rejected him and by their obstinacy made shipwreck of their salvation, any person or thing by which one is (entrapped) drawn into error or sin

G4626.definition: sk pt ,skap' -to apparently a primary verb to dig — dig.

G4627.definition: sk ph ,skaf' -ay a "skiff"(as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel forlanding) — boat.
G4627.usage: anything dug out, hollow vessel, trough, tray, tub, of a boat

G4628.definition: sk los,skel' -os apparently from sk ll (to parch through the idea of leanness) theleg (as lank) — leg.
G4628.usage: the leg, from the hip to the toes inclusive

G4630.definition: Skeu s,skyoo-as' apparently of Latin origin left-handed Scevas (i.e. Scævus), anIsraelite — Sceva.
G4630.usage: Sceva = " mind reader" , a certain chief priest residing at Ephesus

G4631.root: G4632 | σκεῦος | vessel, goods, stuff, sail
G4631.usage: any apparatus, equipment, or furniture, of the utensils or tackling of a ship

G4632.definition: ske os,skyoo' -os of uncertain affinity a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus(literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to theusefulness of the husband]) — goods, sail, stuff, vessel.
G4632.usage: a vessel, an implement, in the plural, household utensils, domestic gear, the tackle and armament of vessels, used specifically of sails and ropes, metaph., a man of quality, a chosen instrument, in a bad sense, an assistant in accomplishing an evil deed

G4633.definition: a tent or cloth hut (literally orfiguratively) — habitation, tabernacle.
G4633.root: G4632 | σκεῦος | vessel, goods, stuff, sail
G4633.usage: tent, tabernacle, (made of green boughs, or skins or other materials), of that well known movable temple of God after the pattern of which the temple at Jerusalem was built

G4634.definition: the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from thecustom of erecting booths for temporary homes) — tabernacles.
G4634.usage: the construction of a tabernacle or tabernacles, the feast of tabernacles this festival was observed by the Jews yearly for seven days, beginning with the 15th of the month Tisri (approx. our Oct.) partly to perpetuate the memory of the time when their ancestors after leaving Egypt dwelt in tents on their way through the Arabian desert, and partly as a season of festivity and joy on the completion of the harvest and the vintage (the festival of ingatherings) In celebrating the festival the Jews were accustomed to construct booths of the leafy branches of trees, — either on the roofs or in the courts of their dwellings, or in the streets and squares, and to adorn them with flowers and fruits of all kinds — under which, throughout the period of the festival, they feasted and gave themselves up to rejoicing.

G4637.definition: to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as amansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle ofold, a symbol of protection and communion) — dwell.
G4637.usage: to fix one's tabernacle, have one's tabernacle, abide (or live) in a tabernacle (or tent), tabernacle, to dwell

G4638.definition: an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God' sresidence), the body (as a tenement for the soul) — tabernacle.
G4638.usage: a tent, a tabernacle, of the temple as God's habitation, of the tabernacle of the covenant, metaph. of the human body as the dwelling of the soul

G4639.definition: ski ,skee' -ah apparently a primary word "shade"or a shadow (literally orfiguratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)) — shadow.
G4639.usage: shadow, shade caused by the interception of light, an image cast by an object and representing the form of that object, a sketch, outline, adumbration

G4640.definition: skirt ,skeer-tah' -o akin to ska r (to skip) to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as thequickening of a fetus) — leap (for joy).

G4641.definition: hard-heartedness, i.e.(specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception — hardness ofheart.

G4642.definition: dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh,severe) — fierce, hard.
G4642.usage: hard, harsh, rough, stiff, of men metaph. harsh, stern, hard, of things violent, rough, offensive, intolerable

G4645.definition: to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn — harden.
G4645.usage: to make hard, harden, metaph., to render obstinate, stubborn, to be hardened, to become obstinate or stubborn

G4646.definition: warped, i.e. winding figuratively,perverse — crooked, froward, untoward.
G4646.usage: crooked, curved, metaph., perverse, wicked, unfair, surly, froward

G4648.usage: to look at, observe, contemplate, to mark, to fix one's eyes upon, direct one's attention to, any one, to look to, take heed to thyself

G4649.definition: a watch (sentry orscout), i.e. (by implication) a goal — mark.
G4649.usage: an observer, a watchman, the distant mark looked at, the goal or end one has in view

G4650.definition: (through the idea of penetrating) todissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, beliberal — disperse abroad, scatter (abroad).
G4650.usage: to scatter, of those who, routed or terror stricken or driven by some other impulses, fly in every direction, to scatter abroad (what others may collect for themselves), or one dispensing blessings literally

G4651.definition: and meaning to pierce) a "scorpion"(from itssting) — scorpion.
G4651.usage: a scorpion, the name of a little animal, somewhat resembling a lobster, which in warm regions lurk, esp. in stone walls it has a poisonous sting in its tail

G4652.definition: opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted — dark, full ofdarkness.
G4652.usage: full of darkness, covered with darkness

G4653.usage: darkness, the darkness due to want of light, metaph. used of ignorance of divine things, and its associated wickedness, and the resultant misery in hell

G4654.usage: to cover with darkness, to darken, to be covered with darkness, be darkened, of heavenly bodies as deprived of light, metaph., of the eyes, of the understanding, of the mind

G4655.usage: darkness, of night darkness, of darkened eyesight or blindness, metaph., of ignorance respecting divine things and human duties, and the accompanying ungodliness and immorality, together with their consequent misery in hell, persons in whom darkness becomes visible and holds sway

G4656.definition: to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively) — be fullof darkness.
G4656.usage: to darken, cover with darkness, metaph. to darken or blind the mind

G4657.definition: what isthrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure) — dung.
G4657.root: G1519 | εἰς | into, to, unto, for, in, on, toward, against, misc
G4657.usage: any refuse, as the excrement of animals, offscourings, rubbish, dregs, of things worthless and detestable

G4658.definition: Sk th s,skoo' -thace probably of foreign origin a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (byimplication) a savage — Scythian.
G4658.usage: Scythian = " rude or rough" , a Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia or modern day Russia, by the more civilised nations of antiquity the Scythians were regarded as the wildest of barbarians

G4659.definition: angry-visaged, i.e.gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance — of a sad countenance.
G4659.root: G3700 | ὀπτάνομαι | see, appear, look, show (one's) self, being seen
G4659.usage: of a sad and gloomy countenance

G4660.definition: sk ll ,skool' -lo apparently a primary verb to flay, i.e. (figuratively) toharass — trouble(self).
G4660.usage: to skin, flay, to rend, mangle, to vex, trouble, annoy, to give one's self trouble, trouble one's self

G4662.definition: worm-eaten, i.e. diseased withmaggots — eaten of worms.

G4663.definition: sk l x,sko' -lakes of uncertain derivation a grub, maggot or earth-worm — worm.
G4663.usage: a worm, spec. that kind which preys upon dead bodies

G4666.usage: myrrh, a bitter gum and costly perfume which exudes from a certain tree or shrub in Arabia and Ethiopia, or is obtained by incisions made in the bark as an antiseptic it was used for embalming

G4667.definition: Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor — Smyrna.
G4667.usage: Smyrna = "myrrh", an Ionian city of Asia Minor, on the Aegean Sea, 40 miles (65 km) north of Ephesus

G4668.usage: of or belonging to Smyrna, an inhabitant of Smyrna

G4669.definition: to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as anarcotic) — mingle with myrrh.
G4669.usage: to be like myrrh, to mix and so flavour with myrrh, wine with myrrh i.e. wine flavoured with myrrh. The ancients used to infuse myrrh into wine to give it a more agreeable fragrance and flavour

G4670.definition: Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place inPalestine — Sodom.
G4670.usage: Sodom = " burning" , a city destroyed by the Lord raining fire and brimstone on it, metaph. Jerusalem Rev. 11 8

G4671.definition: to thee — thee, thine own, thou, thy.

G4672.definition: Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son ofDavid — Solomon.
G4672.usage: Solomon = " peaceful" , the son of David and was the wisest and richest king that ever lived

G4673.definition: a funereal receptacle (urn,coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier — bier.
G4673.usage: an urn or receptacle for keeping the bones of the dead, the funeral couch or bier on which the Jews carried their dead forth to burial

G4675.definition: of thee, thy — X home, thee, thine (own), thou,thy.

G4676.definition: soud rion,soo-dar' -ee-on of Latin origin a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping theperspiration from the face, or binding the face of acorpse) — handkerchief, napkin.
G4676.usage: a handkerchief, a cloth for wiping perspiration from the face and for cleaning the nose and also used in swathing the head of a corpse

G4677.definition: feminine) lily Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), anIsraelitess — Susanna.
G4677.usage: Susanna = " a lily" , one of the women who ministered to Christ

G4678.definition: wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual) — wisdom.
G4678.usage: wisdom, broad and full of intelligence used of the knowledge of very diverse matters, the wisdom which belongs to men, spec. the varied knowledge of things human and divine, acquired by acuteness and experience, and summed up in maxims and proverbs, the science and learning, the act of interpreting dreams and always giving the sagest advice, the intelligence evinced in discovering the meaning of some mysterious number or vision, skill in the management of affairs, devout and proper prudence in intercourse with men not disciples of Christ, skill and discretion in imparting Christian truth, the knowledge and practice of the requisites for godly and upright living, supreme intelligence, such as belongs to God, to Christ, the wisdom of God as evinced in forming and executing counsels in the formation and government of the world and the scriptures

G4680.usage: wise, skilled, expert of artificers, wise, skilled in letters, cultivated, learned, of the Greek philosophers and orators, of Jewish theologians, of Christian teachers, forming the best plans and using the best means for their execution

G4681.definition: Span a,span-ee' -ah probably of foreign origin Spania, a region of Europe — Spain.
G4681.usage: Spain = " scarceness" , the whole peninsula south of the Pyrenees

G4682.definition: through the idea of spasmodic contraction) to mangle, i.e. convlusewith epilepsy — rend, tear.

G4683.definition: meaningto strap or wrap with strips) to swathe (an infant after the Orientalcustom) — wrap in swaddling clothes.
G4683.usage: to wrap in swaddling clothes, of an infant just born

G4684.definition: spatal ,spat-al-ah' -o from spat l (luxury) to be voluptuous — live in pleasure, be wanton.
G4684.usage: to live luxuriously, lead a voluptuous life, (give one's self to pleasure)

G4685.definition: sp ,spah' -o a primary verb to draw — draw (out).

G4686.definition: a coil (spira, "spire", i.e.(figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort also (byanalogy) a squad of Levitical janitors) — band.
G4686.usage: anything rolled into a circle or ball, anything wound, rolled up, folded together, a military cohort, the tenth part of legion, about 600 men i.e. legionaries, if auxiliaries either 500 or 1000, a maniple, or the thirtieth part of a legion, any band, company, or detachment, of soldiers

G4687.definition: (through the idea of extending) toscatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively) — sow(- er), receiveseed.
G4687.usage: to sow, scatter, seed, metaph. of proverbial sayings

G4688.definition: spekoul t r,spek-oo-lat' -ore of Latin origin a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (byextension) life-guardsman) — executioner.
G4688.usage: a spy, scout, under the emperors an attendant and member of the body guard, employed as messengers, watchers, and executioners, the name is transferred to an attendant of Herod Antipas that acted as executioner

G4689.definition: sp nd ,spen' -do apparently a primary verb to pour out as a libation, i.e.(figuratively) to devote (one' s life or blood, as a sacrifice)("spend" — (be ready to) be offered.
G4689.usage: to pour out as a drink offering, make a libation, in the NT to be offered as a libation, fig. used of one whose blood is poured out in a violent death for the cause of God

G4690.definition: something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm" byimplication, offspring specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if keptover for planting) — issue, seed.
G4690.root: G4687 | σπείρω | sow, sower, receive seed
G4690.usage: from which a plant germinates, the seed i.e. the grain or kernel which contains within itself the germ of the future plants, of the grains or kernels sown, metaph. a seed i.e. a residue, or a few survivors reserved as the germ of the next generation (just as seed is kept from the harvest for the sowing), the semen virile, the product of this semen, seed, children, offspring, progeny, family, tribe, posterity, whatever possesses vital force or life giving power, of divine energy of the Holy Spirit operating within the soul by which we are regenerated

G4691.definition: a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) asponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk) — babbler.
G4691.usage: picking up seed, of birds, esp. of the crow or daw that picks up grain in fields, metaph., lounging about the market place and picking up a substance by whatever may chance to fall from the loads of merchandise, hence, beggarly, abject, vile, (a parasite), getting a living by flattery and bufferoonery, an empty talker, babbler

G4692.definition: to "speed"("study", i.e. urge on(diligently or earnestly) by implication, to await eagerly — (make,with) haste unto.
G4692.usage: to haste, make haste, to desire earnestly

G4693.definition: sp laion,spay' -lah-yon neuter of a presumed derivative of sp os (a grotto) a cavern byimplication, a hiding-place or resort — cave, den.

G4694.usage: a rock in the sea, ledge, reef, metaph. of men who by their conduct damage others morally, wreck them as it were

G4695.definition: to stain or soil (literally or figuratively) — defile,spot.

G4696.definition: sp los,spee' -los of uncertain derivation a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively)defect, disgrace — spot.
G4696.usage: a spot, a fault, moral blemish, of base and gluttonous men

G4697.definition: to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively)feel sympathy, to pity — have (be moved with) compassion.
G4697.root: G4698 | σπλάγχνον | bowels, inward affection, tender mercy
G4697.usage: to be moved as to one's bowels, hence to be moved with compassion, have compassion (for the bowels were thought to be the seat of love and pity)

G4698.definition: splangkh' -non probably strengthened from spl n (the "spleen" an intestine(plural) figuratively, pity or sympathy — bowels, inward affection,
G4698.usage: bowels, intestines, (the heart, lungs, liver, etc.), bowels, the bowels were regarded as the seat of the more violent passions, such as anger and love but by the Hebrews as the seat of the tenderer affections, esp. kindness, benevolence, compassion hence our heart (tender mercies, affections, etc.), a heart in which mercy resides

G4699.definition: sp ngos,spong' -gos perhaps of foreign origin a "sponge"— spunge.
